## 1. Welcome to `scSimEvalStudio`

**`scSimEvalStudio`** (version `0.99.3`) is a **point-and-click Shiny web app** built to make single-cell and multiomics simulation benchmarking simple and accessible—even if you are brand new to R.

Instead of writing scripts to run metrics and format dozens of plots, `scSimEvalStudio` gives you a clean browser workspace where you can:

- Try **1-click example datasets** immediately to learn how the app works.
- Upload your own **scRNA-seq**, **scATAC-seq**, or **multiomics** `.rds` datasets (`SingleCellExperiment` or `Seurat`).
- Compare simulators visually on an easy **0 to 1 scale** (where **1.0 = best match** to your real dataset).
- Zoom, pan, customize, and download **600 DPI figures**, **Excel workbooks**, and **reproducible R scripts**.

> **Want the full metric definitions, statistical details, or R programming tutorials?**
> All underlying evaluation methods are documented separately on the **[scSimEval Core Package Documentation](https://kabilanbio.github.io/scSimEval/)**.

```{r workflow-diagram, echo = FALSE, out.width = "100%", fig.cap = "Overview of the 4 simple stages inside scSimEvalStudio: Load Data, Run Evaluation, Compare Rankings, and Explore & Export Results."}

if (!nzchar(wf_img) || !file.exists(wf_img)) {

## 2. Step 1 — Install and Open the App

### Install from Bioconductor

```{r install-bioc, eval = FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages("BiocManager")
}
BiocManager::install("scSimEvalStudio")
```

### Or Install from GitHub

```{r install-github, eval = FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("remotes", quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages("remotes")
}
remotes::install_github("kabilanbio/scSimEval")
remotes::install_github("kabilanbio/scSimEvalStudio")
```

### Launch the Shiny Studio

```{r launch-studio, eval = FALSE}
library(scSimEvalStudio)
launch_scSimEval_app()
```

Your default web browser will open automatically. By default, the app allows uploads up to **10 GiB** so large single-cell `.rds` files can be loaded locally without errors.

---

## 3. Step 2 — Load Data in the Data Hub Tab

When the app opens, click **Data Hub** in the top bar. You have **4 easy options**:

1. **Try a 1-Click Example Dataset (Recommended for Beginners)**
   Choose an included empirical benchmark—such as **Rice Bud** (6 simulators) or **Soybean Root** (3 simulators)—to populate every chart and table in seconds.
2. **Upload Your Own Single-Cell Data (`scRNA-seq` or `scATAC-seq`)**
   Upload your real reference `.rds` file along with one or more simulated `.rds` files. Both `SingleCellExperiment` and `Seurat` `.rds` files are accepted (`Seurat` objects are converted automatically). If your files contain `cell_type` and `batch` columns, extra clustering, batch, and biological signal checks unlock automatically.
3. **Upload Multiomics Data (RNA + ATAC)**
   Choose **Paired** (RNA and ATAC measured in the same cells) or **Unpaired** (measured in separate cells from the same tissue), upload your `.rds` files, and click **Run**.
4. **Reload Previously Saved Results (`.rds` or `.csv`)**
   Already ran a benchmark earlier? Upload your saved `.rds` archive or `.csv` table to view and customize plots instantly without waiting for calculations to run again.

> **Tip for Very Large Datasets:** After configuring your files in **Data Hub**, click **Download R Script** to save a ready-to-run script that you can execute on a lab workstation or HPC server, then upload the saved `.rds` output back into **Data Hub** to explore the plots.

---

## 4. Step 3 — Compare Simulators at a Glance

Open the **Comparative Bubble Matrix** tab to see how your simulators rank:

- **How to Read the Scores:** Every metric is shown on a simple **0.0 to 1.0 scale**, where **closer to 1.0 means a closer match** to your real biological dataset.
- **Comparative Bubble Matrix Figure:** The left bars show overall and category averages; the right grid shows individual metrics as circles. **Bigger circles = better scores**, and a **bold black outline** highlights the top-performing simulator for each metric.
- **Fidelity Leaderboard:** Switch to the second sub-tab for a clean, sortable ranking table that you can download as a `.csv` file.
- **Easy Filtering:** Use the sidebar controls to filter by dataset, modality (`scRNA-seq`, `scATAC-seq`, or `Combined`), specific simulators, or specific categories, and adjust figure width and height before downloading.

---

## 5. Step 4 — Explore Interactive Charts (Visualizations Tab)

The **Visualizations** tab provides **8 focused chart views** so you can inspect your results from every angle:

| Sub-Tab | What It Helps You See |
|:---|:---|
| **1. Evaluation Summary** | Overall and category-level bar charts and radar profiles comparing all simulators side by side. |
| **2. Distribution QC** | Visual checks showing whether simulated library sizes, gene/peak averages, and zero counts match your real data. |
| **3. Metric Heatmap** | Color-coded matrix displaying all simulator scores together in one view (switch between 0–1 scores and raw values). |
| **4. Metric Plots** | Zoom in on any single metric bar chart or compare simulator spread across a category using boxplots. |
| **5. PCA Ordination** | Simple 2D map showing which simulators sit closest to the **Ideal Reference** target. |
| **6. MDS Metric Space** | Visual map grouping simulators that behave similarly across evaluation metrics. |
| **7. Cell Embeddings (UMAP, t-SNE & PCA)** | Side-by-side or overlaid 2D cell plots colored by cell type, batch, or library size, plus a clean cluster quality summary table. |
| **8. Scalability Benchmark** | Compare simulator speed (runtime) and memory usage (RAM) with selectable units (seconds, minutes, MB, GB, or per-core). |

### Interactive Zoom, Pan & Publication Downloads

Every plot panel inside `scSimEvalStudio` includes:

- **Zoom & Pan Toolbar:** Zoom smoothly from **25% to 400%**, drag to pan around large figures, or click **Full View** to inspect plots in fullscreen mode.
- **High-Resolution Downloads:** Save any chart as a **600 DPI JPEG** or **Vector PDF** ready for papers, theses, and posters.
- **1-Click R Script Export:** Download a standalone `ggplot2` R script for any figure if you want to fine-tune colors or labels in R later.

---

## 6. Step 5 — Export Results, Monitor Progress & Get Help

- **Benchmark Results & Export:** Browse, search, and filter the master results table (showing both raw values and 0–1 scores), and download a formatted **Excel workbook (`.xlsx`)**, **`.csv`** table, or full **`.rds`** session backup.
- **Logs:** Watch live progress messages (`INFO`, `WARNING`, `SUCCESS`) while benchmarks run, filter messages by type, or download a `.txt` log file for troubleshooting.
- **Help & Contact:** Access quick in-app tips, file format checklists, and contact details for the development team at ICAR-IASRI, New Delhi.

---

## 7. Quick Verification (For Package Testing)

You can confirm from R that the bundled Shiny app and demo dataset load properly:

```{r verify-app}
library(scSimEvalStudio)

app_dir <- system.file("shiny", "scSimEvalApp", package = "scSimEvalStudio")
dir.exists(app_dir)

app <- shiny::shinyAppDir(app_dir)
class(app)

demo_file <- file.path(app_dir, "data", "demo_benchmark_data.rds")
demo_obj <- readRDS(demo_file)
demo_obj$methods
head(demo_obj$benchmark_summary_table[, c("Method", "Category", "Metric", "Score")], 6)
```
